Steam Locomotives

By: Catherine Rice | Commission

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
It's the largest collection of working narrow gauge steam locomotives in the world and it's nestled at the foot of the majestic Maluti mountains in South Africa.

Unique Selling Point:
Sandstone Estates, in the Eastern Free State, has the largest collection of narrow gauge locomotives and rolling stock in the world.

Summary:
Sandstone Estates in the Eastern Free State attracts international tourists for its collection of steam locomotives. Visitors are able to step into a bygone era and witness these locomotives in action. They are lovingly maintained and many remain in working condition. A 26km long railway line was built on the 8,000 hectare farm, and a "steam festival" is held annually for train enthusiasts. The festival was put on hold this year, as roads in the area are being repaired, but its hoped they will return next year.

Further information:
Gert Jubileus is a train driver who has dedicated his life to preserving the heritage of these locomotives. He describes the inner workings of these machines and the passion he has for them. We also hear from Bryne Keta who is the "fireman". He is responsible for the fire, which heats the water in the boiler to produce steam, and create mechanical motion. He has worked alongside Gert for nine years, and like Gert, his passion for trains dates back to his early childhood. Sandstone Estates is also a working farm.

Script:


VO 1 Before the rest of the country wakes up, in the heart of the Eastern Free State, is a man whose dedication to the past fuels his every move.

VO 2 Train driver Gert Jubileus has been working for hours to prepare this steam locomotive for the tracks…

VO 3 Timeless rituals unfold….gruelling work to balance fire and steam…

UPSOUND Gert (run with subtitles under visuals) Clip 292 / cam 1 Time code: 02:43 I always say when God said with the sweat of your brow you will earn your bread, he was actually thinking of steam locomotives. Because it’s really hard work, it’s a real challenge to keep them running”.

NATSOUND

LINK: Clip 493 / Cam 1 This car has GPS, aircon and is quite comfortable. Modern transportation offers a level of convenience our ancestors could only dream of.

VO 4 Back then…intense physical labour was necessary to power a steam locomotive …

VO 5 In South Africa they were used from the mid-1800s well into the latter part of the twentieth century. …playing a crucial role in building the country.

VO 6 At Sandstone Estates that history is preserved….

NATSOUND Gert explaining to Claire how steam trains work

VO 7 Here, Gert maintains the world’s largest collection of narrow gauge steam locomotives….

UPSOUND Gert Jubileus / Sandstone Estates Railway Manager: I always say that steam locomotives were built by man, but God gave them a soul. They are different, they have a personality, they can be stubborn like humans, don’t want to work with you.

VO 8 This steam locomotive, constructed in Germiston in 1968, is one of the last of the Garratt type locomotives ever built in the world..

NATSOUND Clip 404 Cam 1 Claire: What does that do? Gert “it opens the blower” Claire: Aaaaah
Clip 405 / cam 1 Claire Why would you do that? (you cannot hear Gert’s response and camera goes shaky so not useable)

VO 9 It’s that action that raises steam faster … which in turn heats up the boiler… to prepare for mechanical motion…and transports Gert back to his childhood.

UPSOUND Gert Jubileus / Sandstone Estates Railway Manager (clip 292 / Cam 1). 01:20 My grandfather was a station master on a little station near Kimberley. That’s where it all started.. So, I grew up on steam locomotives, being on the stations between locomotives and it was a way of life.

VO 10 These steam locomotives run on a 26km track specially built for them..

VO 11 Sixty nine steam trains are housed here - some not yet restored. Each one unique.

UPSOUND Gert Jubileus (Cam 1 / clip 292 )Time code: 02:16 The narrow gauge locomotives come from Port Elizabeth, where they operated on the Avontuur line, also from Port Shepstone to Harding.

VO 12 It’s been decades since they were used on South Africa’s railway network.

UPSOUND Gert Time code 1:38 I feared the day it’s going to end. And eventually it did end. For us on the South African Railways. That is when I came to sandstone Estates because here we preserve what I love.

VO 13 That was 21 years ago.

UPSOUND Gert Time code 04:53 SA had a unique collection of steam locomotives. And because we were actually one of the countries that steam ran much later years than overseas so we had the opportunity to preserve locomotives here. Overseas it was something they disposed of.

CLAIRE (Cam 2 / clip 849) Time code 11:17 What is it about these glorious machines that you feel is special to them and no other mode of transport?

UPSOUND Gert 12:17 I think it’s because it’s alive, the smell, the sound, the power. A car you don’t really know when it’s working hard. These locomotives you know when its working hard and you can hear when it struggle. You can hear how the driver handle it.

VO 14 And it’s not just a driver that’s needed to power it…Bryne Keta has been working alongside Gert for the past nine years. It’s his job to fuel the fire….that heats water in the boiler to produce steam.

VO 15 It’s back breaking work in scorching temperatures.

UPSOUND Bryne Keta / Train fireman (Clip 854/ Cam 2) Time code 04:43 You must take care, be sure this thing is going to burn. I can tell you that before it move there, it takes four hours before its ready to go.

Claire: (Clip 857 / Cam 2) Time code: 00:27 Four hours!

UPSOUND: Bryne: Four hour before the steam pressure will go up.

VO 16 He too has loved trains since he was a small boy.

UPSOUND Bryne Keta Clip 854 / Cam 2 Time code 00:19 My mum and my dad used to travel from here to Kuruman. They say when I was three, when I see the train, I just run they say why you going, I say cachoo cachoo, that’s why I say maybe it’s a plan of God, I end up finding myself here in Sandstone.

UPSOUND Bryne 07:24 Especially, When I’m doing my work I like to sing to the Holy One, because I’m excited..

NATSOUND Bryne singing while shovelling coal in the early morning light. (clip 441 / Cam 1)

NATSOUND huffing and puffing clip 367 / cam 1 also clip 380 cam 1 Bryne wiping sweat off his face

VO 17 Bryne and Gert share a camaraderie forged by hours of working together..they both have the same goal…to keep the spirit of steam trains alive..

UPSOUND Bryne Keta: Each and everyone knows how to push himself, especially when you want something, until you see it’s an easy job for me.

VO 18 A job…with magical rewards…and while steam locomotives were replaced by diesel and electric trains many years ago…here…now… in this place…they still reign supreme.

UPSOUND Bryne Time code 8:33 Small people, even me myself I used to come with my children here, my boy he don’t want to jump out of the train, when he see it physically they see this is true. 08:25 They can come here cos Sandstone is all about representing the past to the future.

VO 19 The jewels in the Sandstone heritage collection - two locomotives - called “Lawleys”... they started their life in Mozambique but also worked in South Africa during their 120 year careers. They are the last of just six that remain in the world.

VO 20 The charm and glamour of travelling in coaches like this is undeniable. It was a time when travel was all about style and a sense of adventure. ..

NATSOUND Claire laughing and train hooting Clip 407/ cam 1 Clapping hands and saying “bucket list” and throwing head back laughing

VO 21 These locomotives were collected from Mozambique, Angola, and other parts of South Africa…each one with it’s own unique history.

UPSOUND Claire 03:33 (cam 2) I would never ask a parent which one is their favourite child, but do you have a favourite train?
Gert: Yes, a steam train
Claire: (laughing) All of them in general. Or a particular steam train?
Gert: 04:30 (cam 1) No all of them in general They run in my heart, they are part of me, they raised me from a little boy. It’s what I know. It’s what I live for. .

VO 22 And so he will continue his mission… to preserve the legacy of steam locomotives….a piece of history that will continue to captivate …reverberating into the future.
